:::{#def-convex-function}
#### Convex function

Let $f : \reals^p \to \reals$ be a [function](sets-functions.qmd#def-function).
$f$ is **convex** if
$$
f(t x + (1 - t) y) \le t f(x) + (1 - t) f(y)
$$
for all $x, y \in \reals^p$ and all $t \in [0, 1]$.

:::

::: notes
The point $t x + (1 - t) y$ lies on the line segment from $x$ to $y$,
and the right-hand side is the height of the chord joining
$(x, f(x))$ and $(y, f(y))$ above that point.
So $f$ is convex when every chord lies on or above the graph.
In @exr-convex-chord,
$f(x) = (x - 2)^2$ with $x = 0$, $y = 4$, $t = \tfrac{1}{2}$
gives $f(2) = 0 \le 4$,
which is one instance of the inequality.
:::
